correctness.rationale: For each t, the unit-window intensity is lambda. Two overlapping windows have independent Poisson decomposition, giving exact Charlier cross moments r! lambda^r J_v(t)^r. The L2 expansion and finite 1-lag dependence justify the limiting integrated covariance and CLT. Jensen gives the uniform-intensity lower bound. A nonzero Fourier coefficient of a nonconstant periodic intensity proves strict convexity for every chaos order r>=2 and only affine h may tie. Parseval evaluates the factorial-second-moment penalty exactly. Reproducibility script verify.py reports 324 finite exact and numerical diagnostics; finite tests are not infinite proof.

value.rationale: The motivating sampler literature explicitly asks whether oscillatory baseline intensity affects efficiency. The simultaneous minimization of variance for all nonlinear count observables with a sharp affine exception is a structural answer, while the closed-form nonnegative spectral penalty supplies a natural precise effect size for estimating second factorial moments. This distinction is not a routine normalization artifact and does not follow from optimizing the linear count alone.
